scope: The late nineteenth-century blacksmith forge at the Obadjiwan trading post, with its full measured timber enclosure, steep gable roof, little west door canopy, single adjacent window and masonry stack at the south gable.
imageryReview: Reviewed the original Qualla set first. The exact 1876 McLaughlin waterfront photograph has native public-domain tags and an item-specific expiry record. It supports the overall late nineteenth-century timber post appearance. The specific forge elevations and measured plan follow the excavation report.
geometryBasis: A 7.10 m by 6.30 m archaeological envelope at the mapped forge center. Historical turnover and the surviving mapped exhibit make the exact position approximate.
sectionBasis: The excavated timber building is one storey with a gable roof, centred west door under a canopy, one adjacent west window and a south gable fireplace. The report measures the rubble fireplace base at 2.05 m by 1.37 m.
